result:
The proposed solution's key step is not valid, so I reject its final answer of 0.

The argument claims that complex conjugation on SU(3) induces an orientation-preserving isometry of N_{k,l}, and that this forces the Dirac and odd signature spectra to be symmetric about 0. That does not follow. An orientation-preserving isometry preserves the spectrum but does not reflect it. Spectral symmetry would need an orientation-reversing isometry, and an orientation-preserving isometry gives no such constraint.

Complex conjugation also sends S^1_{k,l} to S^1_{-k,-l}, so in general it is not even an automorphism of N_{k,l} itself.

The last step, that the "torsion/characteristic terms cancel", is asserted without any computation.

I am working from memory of the Crowley–Goette–Nordström ν̄-invariant and its computations on homogeneous nearly-parallel G2-structures, not from a derivation. As I recall, the two structures on an Aloff-Wallach space have nonzero ν̄ values, and their absolute value is nonzero. On that basis 0 is not the expected answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
